How Plants Make Food

Photosynthesis is the process plants use to turn light into chemical energy. It happens mostly in the leaves, where cells are packed with chloroplasts.

Inside each chloroplast, the pigment chlorophyll absorbs sunlight. That energy then powers a chain of reactions that split water molecules apart.

The plant keeps the hydrogen and releases the oxygen as a waste product. It combines the hydrogen with carbon dioxide to build sugars for growth.

These sugars feed the plant and, indirectly, nearly every animal on Earth. Without photosynthesis the food chain would collapse within a single season.
